summary: Return the length of the longest well-formed parentheses substring.
mainInsight: Use a stack of indices with a base marker: push the index of every '('; on ')' pop. If the stack becomes empty push the current index as the new base; otherwise the valid substring ends here and starts just after the new top.
canonicalApproach: Stack of indices with a base

approaches.name: Dynamic programming
approaches.summary: dp[i] = longest valid ending at i.

approaches.name: Stack of indices with a base
approaches.summary: Push -1 first; track the last unmatched index.

approaches.name: Two counter passes
approaches.summary: Left-to-right and right-to-left counting of opens/closes.

personalSolution.approach: Stack of indices with a base
personalSolution.notes: Optimal in time; the two-pass counter version uses O(1) space.

promptVariants: What do you store on the stack for Longest Valid Parentheses?
options: Indices of unmatched characters, with -1 as the initial base
The characters themselves, popped on a match
Counts of '(' seen so far in the string
Lengths of the valid substrings found so far
cards.answer: Indices of unmatched characters, with -1 as the initial base
cards.explanation: The index below the top marks where the current valid run begins; -1 handles a valid prefix starting at index 0.

promptVariants: What does the element below the top of the stack represent?
cards.answer: The stack holds indices of '(' that are still unmatched plus one base index (the last position that cannot be part of a valid substring). For any current ')' that matches, the valid substring ends at i and starts at stack[-1] + 1 after the pop, giving length i - stack[-1].
cards.explanation: Pushing i when the stack empties resets the base.
Each index is pushed and popped at most once.

promptVariants: What is the stack's worst-case size and how can it be reduced to O(1)?
How large can the index stack get, and how would you get O(1) extra space?
cards.answer: O(n) (e.g. all '('). Two left-to-right and right-to-left passes with open/close counters achieve O(1) extra space: reset counters when closes exceed opens, record 2 * min when they are equal.

promptVariants: Why `if not stack: stack.append(i)` after the pop, and what does `cur_len = i - stack[-1]` measure?
What is the `elif stack:` condition for?
cards.answer: A ')' pops the most recent '(' or the base marker. If the stack becomes empty that ')' was unmatched, so its index becomes the new base. Otherwise the matched substring runs from stack[-1] + 1 to i, whose length is i - stack[-1]. The `elif stack` condition is always true because the base keeps the stack non-empty.
keyPoints: Pop the match or the base
cards.explanation: The base never gets popped permanently.

promptVariants: Which substring is the longest valid?
cards.explanation: The first ')' is unmatched, the next four characters form '()()', and the last ')' is unmatched.

incorrectOptionExplanations.6: The unmatched outer ')' break the string.
